summary: Intro discovery focused on PLG quickstart: free credits, time-to-first-token, hosted vs dedicated tradeoffs. Sable Tech is early evaluation, primary concerns are latency for customer-facing features, data residency, and ops velocity. Agreed to pilot using hosted API with plan to evaluate Dedicated if latency/cost needs require it.
transcript:
00:00 Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Jordan from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account, with me is Priya our solutions engineer. quick intro?
00:08 Marcus Reed: Marcus here, CTO at Sable Tech, we build customer-facing search and recommendation features, latency is a big deal for us.
00:13 Aisha Khan: Hi, Aisha, ML eng, i'll own eval and pilot.
00:17 Priya Shah: great, quick agenda: understand your stack and success criteria, show how quickstart and free credits work, discuss hosted vs dedicated/private for production.
00:28 Jordan Lee: we usually offer free credits and a self-serve quickstart so teams can get first token in minutes, curious what your timeline looks like?
00:34 Marcus Reed: timeline is pretty soon, we want a small pilot in 2 weeks, decision within a month. primary questions: can we get up and running quickly, how does latency compare, and what are the security constraints.
00:44 Priya Shah: totally, so for quickstarts we do REST + SDK, you can create an API key, use a sample prompt and see time-to-first-token in under a minute. free credits cover the initial token usage and we have starter templates for embeddings and chat.
00:55 Noah Kim: what about egress and VPC? our infra team wants VPC peering or private deployment for PII.
01:02 Priya Shah: for pilot we recommend hosted API with KMS integration for keys and configurable retention; if you need private network we have Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem). Dedicated is reserved GPU capacity if you need consistent throughput.
01:15 Aisha Khan: curious on costs — does hosted blow up if we have lots of inference?
01:19 Jordan Lee: great question. hosted is pay-as-you-go and ideal for quick evaluation and PLG. Dedicated reduces per-token cost at scale with reserved capacity. Redwood Optimize gives recommendations on batching and quantization.
01:32 Marcus Reed: ok, and latency — we care about 200ms p95 for short chat completions and sub-50ms for embeddings calls in our pipeline, is that realistic?
01:40 Priya Shah: embeddings sub-50ms depends on region and model size; for smaller models and our edge configs it's achievable. For the chat p95 200ms, that often pushes you toward dedicated with GPU pools tuned for low latency and KV cache warmup. we can run benchmarks during pilot.
01:58 Aisha Khan: what's involved in the quickstart? we prefer self-serve steps we can hand to devs.
02:03 Priya Shah: quickstart steps: sign up, get API key, sample prompts in SDK, run a couple of requests, we'll give a Postman collection and a sample node/python snippet. in our experience time-to-first-token often <5 minutes for devs who already have cloud creds.
02:18 Jordan Lee: i'll share the quickstart deck and free credits link after the call.
02:25 Marcus Reed: security: are you SOC 2 / do you support SSO/SAML and audit logs?
02:30 Priya Shah: Redwood is SOC 2 compliant, SSO/SAML and SCIM supported for teams, we have per-request audit logs and customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for Private. for hosted, we do encryption at rest and in transit and can configure retention.
02:46 Noah Kim: if we start on hosted and then move to Private, how painful is the migration?
02:51 Priya Shah: we designed the API to be consistent across hosted/dedicated/private, so code changes are minimal — mostly config and network. for Private there's some infra work (VPC, KMS). we can plan a migration path in the pilot.
03:02 Marcus Reed: what about model catalog and controlling versions?
03:06 Priya Shah: you can pin model versions, rollout policies, and do canary deployments. Redwood also offers quantized model variants if you want cost/latency tradeoffs.
03:15 Aisha Khan: any gotchas on tokenization and billing?
03:18 Jordan Lee: tokens billed per request; we give a token breakdown in console so you can see per-route costs. caching prefixes and batching recommended to lower cost.
03:27 Marcus Reed: competitors? we're also talking to MajorCloud AI and doing some in-house microservice.
03:31 Jordan Lee: understood — we'll surface concrete latency/cost numbers from our benchmarks.
03:35 Priya Shah: for the pilot we propose three tests: (1) quickstart smoke on hosted to validate integration and time-to-first-token, (2) latency benchmark with your real prompts against hosted and a dedicated config, (3) security review with SSO/KMS details.
03:52 Marcus Reed: sounds good. who will own the benchmarks on Redwood side?
03:56 Priya Shah: i'll run the benchmarks and share a spreadsheet — will include p95/p50, token counts, instance types.
04:04 Aisha Khan: will you provide example Dockerfile if we want to run local inference later?
04:08 Priya Shah: yes, i'll include a sample Dockerfile and a recommended quantization profile.
04:12 Jordan Lee: budget — what's your expected spend for pilot?
04:16 Marcus Reed: small, maybe a few hundred to validate; if we like results we can move to a month-long pilot at higher commit.
04:23 Noah Kim: retention and logs — need 1 year of audit logs for compliance.
04:28 Priya Shah: we can enable longer retention as an add-on for hosting, or for Private it's fully controlled.
04:33 Marcus Reed: great. any blockers from your side, Aisha?
04:36 Aisha Khan: just want the sample prompts and benchmark template so we can run quickly.
04:40 Jordan Lee: action recap: i'll send quickstart + credits, Priya will share benchmark and dockerfile, Marcus will confirm scope. we'll schedule pilot kickoff week of 2026-03-15.
04:51 Marcus Reed: thanks all. quick note — if dedicated is needed we may discuss reserved capacity since consistent latency is important.
04:57 Priya Shah: understood. we'll include dedicated sizing options in the benchmark sheet.
05:02 Jordan Lee: thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email, end call.
05:06 [end of recording]
